title: Light Image Viewer for Mac - Belvue for Mac
description: Open one image and flip through the whole folder with the arrow keys. Belvue is a light Mac image viewer in Finder order, with no ads and no tracking.
h1: A light image viewer for Mac
tagline: Open one image, flip through the whole folder with the arrow keys
summary: Belvue is a light image viewer for the Mac. Open a single image and the rest of its folder is ready to browse with the arrow keys, in the same order as Finder.
It is for anyone looking for a Mac image viewer to browse folders of photos, screenshots or scans, even with thousands of images.
Your images and file paths stay on your Mac, with no ads and no tracking.
overview: Preview and Quick Look are fine for one picture, but going through a whole folder often means opening images one by one. In Belvue you open one image and the next one appears right away when you press the arrow key. Folders with thousands of images use the same natural order as Finder, and the list follows changes in the folder.

In a Mac image viewer, the useful parts are the small ones. Belvue has a thumbnail strip, zoom, pan, full screen and an information panel with EXIF details. You can also pick images as you flip with the P key, then act on all your picks at once. Copying the current image is a plain Command-C.

features.h: Open one, browse the whole folder
features.p: Open one image and move through its folder with the arrow keys. The next image appears right away, and the order matches Finder, including folders with thousands of images.

features.h: Thumbnail strip, zoom and full screen
features.p: A thumbnail strip, zoom, pan and full screen are built in, along with an information panel that shows EXIF details.
Press P to pick images while you browse. With Belvue Pro you can move, copy or send all picks to the Trash at once, with undo, and the original is never changed when you copy.

features.h: Convert to JPEG, PNG or HEIC
features.p: Belvue Pro converts picked images to JPEG, PNG or HEIC and creates a new file, so the original stays as it was.
Images and file paths never leave your Mac. Belvue has no ads and no tracking, and its only network connection is to the App Store for Belvue Pro.

specs.v: JPEG, PNG, HEIC, RAW and more
Natural order, the same as Finder
Thumbnail strip, zoom, pan, full screen, EXIF panel, Copy with Command-C, recent folders
No ads, no tracking; network connection only to the App Store
Batch move, copy and Trash for picks, conversion to JPEG, PNG or HEIC, sharing, Open With, extra backgrounds

limits: Because of the Mac App Store sandbox, macOS gives Belvue access only to the image you open. To browse the rest of its folder, Belvue asks you to allow that folder once. If you decline, the image you opened still opens, but you cannot flip through its siblings.
Batch move, copy, Trash, conversion, sharing, Open With and the extra backgrounds need Belvue Pro. Viewing, browsing and picking do not.
Belvue is an image viewer, not a photo library or an editor, and it does not edit your images.
It is a Mac app only.

faq.q: Which Mac image viewer lets me browse a whole folder?
faq.a: Belvue is a light Mac image viewer. Open one image and flip through the rest of the folder with the arrow keys, in the same order as Finder, even with thousands of images.

faq.q: Why does Belvue ask me to allow a folder?
faq.a: The Mac App Store sandbox lets an app read only the file you opened. Belvue asks once for access to that folder so it can show the other images. If you decline, the opened image still displays.

faq.q: Which image formats does it open?
faq.a: JPEG, PNG, HEIC, RAW and more.
Viewing, browsing and picking work without Pro. Belvue Pro is optional and adds batch move, copy and Trash for your picks, conversion to JPEG, PNG or HEIC, sharing, Open With and extra backgrounds.

faq.q: Does Belvue send my images anywhere?
faq.a: No. Images and file paths never leave your Mac. Belvue has no ads and no tracking, and its only network connection is to the App Store for Belvue Pro.
